article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 50% Indica / 50% Sativa
Genetics: Purple Chocolope × Honey Banana
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: 1%
Terpene Profile: Terpinolene, ocimene, myrcene
Primary Flavors: Ripe banana, honey, chocolate, coffee
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early October
Indoor Yield: 425–595 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Bruised Bananas approaches dessert-style cannabis from a direction few fruit strains attempt. Ripe banana and honey dominate the opening aroma, but instead of finishing with more tropical sweetness, the profile turns toward cocoa, roasted coffee, earth, and subtle spice. The effect can resemble the sensory contrast of a chocolate-covered banana rather than conventional candy weed, and purple coloration in selected plants gives the cultivar an appearance that fits its unusual name. DNA Genetics created the strain from Purple Chocolope × Honey Banana, deliberately joining a cerebral, chocolate-influenced parent with one of the breeder’s sweeter and more resinous banana lines.

That genetic contrast carries directly into the experience and the garden. Bruised Bananas is a balanced hybrid capable of beginning with clear euphoria, creative energy, and social engagement before gradually settling into warmer physical relaxation. Plants are vigorous, highly productive, and capable of developing dense, resin-coated flowers within an 8–10-week bloom. Indoor yields can approach 21 ounces per square meter under strong conditions, while outdoor plants may exceed 800 grams each. For growers looking for a banana variety with genuine flavor depth rather than simple sweetness, this hybrid offers chocolate, fruit, resin, and production in unusually equal measure.
Genetics and Lineage

The official DNA Genetics pedigree is Purple Chocolope × Honey Banana. Purple Chocolope represents the brighter, more cerebral side of the family and builds upon the famous Chocolope tradition. Chocolope became one of DNA Genetics’ defining cultivars through its chocolate, coffee, earthy sweetness, vigorous growth, and stimulating effects. Purple Chocolope adds proprietary purple genetics to that foundation, bringing greater coloration and additional depth while preserving much of the chocolate-oriented personality and energetic character associated with the Chocolope family.

Honey Banana supplies the heavier fruit and resin component. DNA Genetics developed Honey Banana from Strawberry Banana × Honey Boo Boo. Strawberry Banana contributes sweet tropical fruit, ripe banana, resin, and substantial cannabinoid potential, while Honey Boo Boo brings Bubba Kush and Captain Krypt OG influence into the family. Those Kush-oriented genetics deepen the physical effects and add earthier, more relaxing qualities beneath the fruit. Honey Banana later became especially respected for concentrate production, reinforcing the resin potential carried into Bruised Bananas.

The offspring sit almost exactly between those two parental directions. Purple Chocolope pushes growth, chocolate, coffee, creativity, and cerebral energy, while Honey Banana contributes dense flower, tropical sweetness, honey, and a calmer physical finish. DNA Genetics describes the resulting cultivar as a balanced indica-sativa hybrid rather than forcing it into one category. That classification makes sense both genetically and experientially: Bruised Bananas can show tall, vigorous growth while still producing heavy buds and an increasingly relaxed body effect.
Effects and Experience

The opening phase tends to favor mental activity. A few inhalations can produce a noticeable lift in mood accompanied by clearer focus, conversational energy, and an increased desire to engage with music, art, or other creative work. The effect is upbeat without necessarily becoming frantic, and moderate doses may remain functional enough for an afternoon project or relaxed social setting. Purple Chocolope contributes strongly here, giving the cultivar more cerebral movement than its dense, purple-tinged flowers might initially suggest.

Physical relaxation develops more gradually. As the cerebral peak settles, warmth spreads through the body and muscular tension begins to feel less prominent. The mind generally remains engaged while the body becomes calmer, creating a middle stage where stimulation and relaxation coexist rather than replacing one another. Larger servings move the experience more decisively toward the Honey Banana side, bringing heavier physical comfort and making the strain increasingly appropriate for evening use.

With breeder-listed THC around 15–20%, Bruised Bananas falls below the extreme potency figures attached to many modern weed strains , but the experience should not be dismissed as mild. The combined cannabinoid and terpene profile can still feel substantial, particularly for consumers with limited tolerance. Excessive intake may lead to dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental haze, or temporary anxiety. Measured dosing tends to preserve the strain’s most distinctive quality—the ability to remain mentally bright while the body gradually relaxes.
Medical Benefits

The balanced progression may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want a cultivar that does not begin with immediate sedation. The early uplift can make stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less dominant while preserving enough clarity for light activities. As the experience develops, the physical component may help reduce awareness of muscular tightness or everyday discomfort without forcing the consumer into complete inactivity.

Larger doses can produce a more pronounced calming effect, potentially making the cultivar useful later in the day when relaxation becomes more desirable. Appetite may increase, and the body can feel substantially quieter as the Honey Banana influence becomes more apparent. People sensitive to THC should still use caution because the cerebral beginning can become overstimulating if too much is consumed before the slower physical effects emerge.

Bruised Bananas is commonly associated with terpinolene, ocimene, and myrcene, a combination consistent with its sweet, herbal, fruity, and gently relaxing aromatic character. These compounds help shape the sensory experience but should not be treated as medical treatments on their own. Consumers using marijuana therapeutically should consider laboratory results from the specific harvest, personal tolerance, medications, and previous responses to THC and CBD rather than assuming every plant will produce identical effects.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Banana is unmistakable but rarely isolated. The fruit smells ripe and creamy rather than green or sharply tropical, and honey adds a dense sweetness that gives the bouquet almost syrup-like weight. Citrus can appear around the edges, adding a brighter accent that keeps the top end from becoming overly rich. In certain phenotypes, the combination can resemble banana bread, banana cake, or a smoothie sweetened with honey.

Purple Chocolope adds the darker half of the profile. Chocolate, cocoa, coffee, earth, and mild spice emerge after the flower is broken apart, creating an unusually savory contrast to the fruit. Some plants lean heavily toward the banana-honey side, while others display a clearer roasted-coffee or chocolate character. A faint skunky or diesel-like pungency may also appear underneath, particularly in resin-heavy expressions.

Flavor generally begins sweeter than the raw aroma. Banana and honey arrive first on the inhale, followed by cream, citrus, and mild vanilla before coffee, cocoa, and earth become more obvious through the exhale. Vaporization tends to preserve the lighter fruit and honey notes most clearly, while combustion emphasizes chocolate, spice, and the deeper earthy finish. A slow dry and patient cure are particularly important because the cultivar’s appeal depends on keeping both the tropical and roasted aromatic layers intact.
Growing Information

Bruised Bananas combines substantial vigor with a relatively forgiving growth pattern. Indoors, DNA Genetics describes plants reaching roughly three to five feet depending on vegetative time and training, while outdoor specimens can exceed six feet when given unrestricted roots and strong sunlight. Branching is robust enough to support considerable flower weight, and the cultivar responds well to topping, Screen of Green, and other canopy-management techniques. Its hybrid structure allows growers to spread the plant horizontally without losing the vertical energy inherited from Purple Chocolope.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 8–10 weeks, with breeder-listed yields of 15–21 ounces per square meter, equivalent to roughly 425–595 g/m². Flowers become dense and increasingly resinous as maturity approaches, and some plants develop pronounced purple coloration. Good airflow and moderate late-flower humidity are important because heavy buds can trap moisture even on otherwise vigorous plants. The breeder considers the cultivar suitable for less experienced growers, although training and canopy management become increasingly useful when trying to reach the upper end of its production potential.

Outdoor harvest generally arrives around early October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Under strong conditions, mature plants can produce around 800 grams each or more, particularly when provided with rich soil, direct sun, ample root space, and a long vegetative period. The heavy trichome production also gives the strain strong potential for dry sift, ice-water hash , and rosin . Growers selecting multiple plants may want to judge banana intensity, chocolate character, resin density, purple coloration, branch strength, and yield together rather than choosing a keeper on size alone.
FAQ
What strains make Bruised Bananas?

Bruised Bananas was bred by DNA Genetics from Purple Chocolope × Honey Banana. Honey Banana comes from Strawberry Banana × Honey Boo Boo, while Purple Chocolope brings Chocolope-family chocolate, coffee, cerebral energy, and purple genetic influence.
Is Bruised Bananas indica or sativa?

DNA Genetics classifies Bruised Bananas as a balanced hybrid with approximately equal indica and sativa influence. The effects reflect that balance, beginning with cerebral uplift and creativity before developing into a calmer physical state.
How much THC does Bruised Bananas have?

DNA Genetics lists THC at approximately 15–20% with low CBD, generally below 1%. Final cannabinoid levels can vary according to phenotype, cultivation environment, harvest timing, curing, and laboratory methodology.
What does Bruised Bananas taste like?

The primary flavor combines ripe banana and honey with chocolate, coffee, citrus, earth, and mild spice. Some phenotypes lean strongly toward tropical sweetness, while others express a darker cocoa-and-coffee character from Purple Chocolope.
How long does Bruised Bananas take to flower?

Indoor flowering takes approximately 8–10 weeks. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around early October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates, although latitude and seasonal conditions can alter the exact harvest date.
Final Thoughts on Bruised Bananas

Bruised Bananas succeeds because its two parents contribute flavors that rarely appear together with this much clarity. Honey Banana supplies ripe fruit, honeyed sweetness, dense flower, and resin, while Purple Chocolope brings chocolate, coffee, color, and a livelier cerebral personality. The result avoids the common problem of banana strains becoming one-dimensional by giving the fruit a darker roasted background.

The cultivation package is equally impressive. An 8–10-week flowering period, indoor yields reaching roughly 425–595 g/m², outdoor production around 800 grams per plant or more, vigorous branching, and substantial trichome development give the cultivar serious production value. Its relative resilience makes it approachable, while training techniques allow experienced growers to push canopy efficiency and harvest weight further.

For consumers, the experience completes the balance suggested by the genetics. Creative euphoria and focus define the beginning, warm body relaxation develops afterward, and the flavor moves from honeyed banana into cocoa, coffee, citrus, and earth. Bruised Bananas stands out within DNA Genetics’ fruit-focused catalog because it combines dessert sweetness with genuinely complex cannabis character rather than relying on banana flavor alone.
